body.statement: For every \(\lambda\in[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\), \(t\in(0,1]\), and \(\sigma_0^2,\sigma_1^2>0\), the explicit construction in \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}support\text{-}witness}\) belongs to \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{legal}}\). For all sufficiently large \(n\), \(\rho_{n,k_n^{\dagger}}=\rho_{n,0}\), whereas \[d_n(k_n^{\dagger},0)^2\ge B_n^2(a_n^{\dagger})^2\longrightarrow D_\infty=2\sigma_0^2\left\{\lambda^{-1}-\frac{\lambda}{[\lambda+2t(1-\lambda)]^2}\right\}>0.\] Consequently \(\omega^{\star}(0)\ge\sqrt{D_\infty}>0\): exact leading-MSE ties need not be ATE-coordinate ties even with no covariates, convex squared-error ranking, bounded outcomes, and legal nested prefixes.
body.justification: The explicit witness independently tests the prefix geometry and shows that equal leading risk does not coerce equality of the selected ATE coordinate.
body.gap: Leeb and Poetscher give generic model-selection nonuniformity; this result embeds a tied-risk separation inside Yang, Li, Wu, and Yang's legal external-control prefix class with the actual influence score and tie breaker.
body.consumer: Any interval claimed uniformly over the legal prefix class must protect more than one separated ATE coordinate at an exact risk tie.
